eval_pdf.footer: Policy Analyzer · local AI evaluation · synthetic data, measured on the firewall
eval_pdf.method: The score of each scenario goes from 0 to 100 and combines two questions: "is the answer useful?" (effectiveness, weight %s) and "does it arrive in time and fit in the firewall?" (performance, weight %s). I gave more weight to effectiveness because a fast wrong answer is worse than none: it misleads the administrator. Effectiveness is measured without an AI judge, only with objective rules (plugin validation, Portuguese, anchoring in the data, key facts, size and stability), so two models are always compared with the same ruler.

glossary_items.validacao: Plugin validation (%d): the same check the plugin makes in production (sections, JSON Schema, 1st line MAPPING/TYPE, citations). If it fails, the module cannot even show the answer; if it passes only after the correction, it cost a second call (score 0.6).
glossary_items.idioma: Strict pt-BR (%d): texts that become e-mails, PDFs or dashboards must not mix in English; the same rule rejects the answer in production.
glossary_items.raciocinio: No leaked reasoning (%d): planning notes ("Okay, the user wants...") in the middle of the answer were the failure of the early hours of Nov 9; a model that leaks its reasoning is no good for published text.
glossary_items.ancoragem: Anchoring (%d): every address, port, CVE, host or citation of the answer must exist in the input. Inventing an IP in a security report is worse than leaving it out: it loses 25 points per item, and unsafe advice zeroes it.
glossary_items.cobertura: Key facts (%d): every fixture has the list of what a good answer must say (e.g. the exposed port 445). It measures whether the model understood the case, not only whether it wrote nicely.
glossary_items.formato: Format and size (%d): the size requested by the scenario (sentences or words); an answer cut by num_predict scores 0, because the reader gets half a text.
glossary_items.estabilidade: Stability (%d): with 2+ repetitions, I compare the spread of the scores and whether the decision (MAPPING, TYPE, incident actions) repeats. A model that is right once and wrong the next time is not reliable.
glossary_items.time: Typical time p50 (%d) and worst case p95 (%d): compared with the budget of the scenario (the timeout of the local_only route). The p50 says how normal use will feel; the p95 says whether there will be timeouts. The p50 scale is logarithmic: every time the time doubles, it loses the same amount.
glossary_items.tps: Generation in tokens/s (%d): %d tok/s or more scores 100 (a little above reading speed).
glossary_items.ttft: First token (%d): load + reading the prompt; it is the wait before anything shows up.
glossary_items.ram: Resident RAM (%d): up to %d GiB scores 100, %d GiB or more scores 0 (the firewall needs free memory for Suricata, ZFS and the filter itself).
glossary_items.carga: Host load (%d): load average during inference, measured against the share given to the model: up to the number of threads of the jail scores 100; at the limit of the bench guard (threads + %s, at most the host cores) it scores 0 and the bench pauses.
glossary_items.indication: Indication: "recommended" = effectiveness >= %d, p95 within the budget, no timeout, no answer in another language or with reasoning, and at least 2 answers; "promising" = effectiveness >= %d (there is a hint, worth more samples); the rest is "not recommended". Confidence grows with the number of runs and falls with the spread (95%% CI = 1.96 × deviation / square root of n).

conclusions.weakest: The weakest point was "%s" (average %s of 1): %s. That is where I would start investigating before trusting this model.

weak_why.validacao: the format requested by the module (sections, JSON, 1st line) is not right at the first attempt
weak_why.idioma: English gets mixed in, which fails published texts
weak_why.raciocinio: the model writes its own reasoning into the answer
weak_why.ancoragem: it cites addresses, ports or CVEs that were not in the data (hallucination)
weak_why.cobertura: it leaves out central facts of the case
weak_why.formato: it misses the requested size or is cut by num_predict
weak_why.estabilidade: the repetitions disagree with each other

conclusions.tps_others: , against %s tokens/s for the median of the other models measured
conclusions.tps_why: . On the N100 the speed depends mostly on the ACTIVE parameters per token: that is why a 30B MoE with 3B active can be faster than a dense 8B model.
conclusions.ram: It took %s GiB of RAM; about %s GiB are left for the firewall (I consider 8 GiB or more enough headroom). %s
conclusions.ram_tight: It is tight: with Suricata and ZFS memory may run short.
conclusions.slow: It exceeded the time budget (p95 above the route timeout) in: %s. In these scenarios the answer would not arrive in production without raising the timeout or sending it to the queue.
conclusions.thinks: This model always reasons before answering; every answer pays for the reasoning tokens, which explains much of the time. For published texts I prefer models without reasoning.
conclusions.leads: Today it leads the history in: %s.
conclusions.low_confidence: There is a favorable hint with low confidence in %s: I would evaluate again with more repetitions (start avaliacao only=%s reps=5 reeval) before deciding.

model.components_note: Each column goes from 0 to 1 (average of the repetitions): Plugin (validation), Strict (pt-BR), No (leaked reasoning), Anchoring, Key (facts), Format and Stability. Examples of failures in this evaluation:
model.history: Comparison with the history (every model measured on the firewall)

charts.heading: Charts
charts.per_scenario_note: Grouped bars: effectiveness, performance and the composite score of each scenario. When effectiveness is high and performance low, the model is right but slow; the opposite is worse.
charts.scatter: Effectiveness × performance per scenario (number = row of the results table)
charts.scatter_note: The top right corner is the ideal. Above the dashed line (effectiveness %d) the scenario can be "recommended"; the ring marks the ones that were. A point high up and to the left is a good model that is slow for this scenario: a candidate for the queue.
charts.ranges_note: Gray line: minimum to maximum; bar: p50 to p95; circle: p50; red tick: the budget (route timeout). The farther from the red tick, the more headroom the scenario has.
charts.ranking: Ranking of the models by the average score of the scenarios
charts.map: Map of the models: average effectiveness × average performance (number = ranking position)
charts.map_note: Each point is a model (average of the scenarios). The ring marks the model of this report.
charts.cost: Cost on the firewall: RAM and load
charts.cost_note: RAM: memory of the loaded model (/api/ps). Load: the p95 of the host load average during the runs; the guard pauses above %s with the share of this report.

bench_md.title: # Local AI catalog of the Policy Analyzer
bench_md.intro: Generated by `configctl policyanalyzer ai_bench_report` on %s from `/var/db/policyanalyzer/ai-bench.db` (plan %s #%s, %s). Measured on the firewall itself, one request at a time, with the plugin pipeline ("Local only" preset with the model of each round, validation + 1 correction, JSON Schema, map/reduce).
bench_md.rounds_head: | Round | Name | State | Start | End | Steps (done/error/skipped) |
bench_md.results_note: Rounds matrix + repeatability (+ imported). Format = share that passed the plugin validation on the 1st answer / after the correction; language = pt-BR heuristic (or the language asked by the reports module).
bench_md.results_head: | Scenario | Model | Runs | Tokens in/out | Run (s) p50 / max | 1st token (s) | Format 1st / after | Language | Attempts | Parts | Timeouts | Score (0-3) | Serves? |
bench_md.serves_note: Criterion of "Serves?": **yes** = format and language ≥ 90 % after the correction, score ≥ 2 and time within the limit (synchronous: ≤ 300 s at p90; queue/background: ≤ 1800 s, no timeout); **partial** = one of the three fails; **no** = two or more.
bench_md.quality_note: **Quality score (automatic, 0–3):** starts at 3; −1 if the format fails even after the correction; −1 if the language is wrong; −1 if the answer cites a CVE or port that is not in the data sent, a `[section: …]` citation of a missing section or unsafe advice (turn off the firewall/Suricata, allow everything); −1 if it was cut by num_predict; 0 without an answer (error/timeout).
bench_md.json_head: | Scenario | Model | Runs | Valid JSON/1st line | Format after correction | Ids outside the list |

cost_rows.warm: Load with the model already resident (s)

bench_md.impact_note: Samples every %d s (%d s in the threads round): load, CPU, temperature, free memory, RTT/loss of the active WAN (dpinger), ping to 1.1.1.1 and Suricata drops (stats.log). Guard limits: loss > %.0f %%, RTT > %.0f ms or load > %.1f for %d samples in a row = pause (the load limit is the number of threads of the jail + %.1f, at most the number of cores of the host).
